summary.text: Ken Kerr is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 3, in Frederick County, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A longtime Frederick Community College faculty member, he has served in the House since January 2019 and is vice chair of the Government, Labor, and Elections Committee.

paragraphs.text: Kerr was born in Boston and graduated from Woodlawn High School in Baltimore County in 1975.

He earned an A.A. from Frederick Community College in 1978, a B.A. in music from Hood College in 1981, an M.S. in professional writing from Towson University in 1995, and a Ph.D. in education from Morgan State University in 2003.

He taught at Harford Community College and Wor-Wic Community College before joining Frederick Community College in 1999, where he chaired the English Department from 2011 to 2017 and served as interim dean of arts and sciences in 2015-2016.
Kerr was a member of the Frederick County Board of Education from 2016 to 2018 and was first elected to the House of Delegates in 2018.
He serves on the Government, Labor, and Elections Committee, where he is vice chair and chairs the Government Operations and Ethics Subcommittee, and on the Rules and Executive Nominations Committee.
